To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the electrochemical and spectroscopic properties of viologen radical ions are affected by intramolecular association.
the viologen dimer radical cation and trimer radical cations are stable and can be generated electrochemically and that the viologens form dimers and trimers in solution.
the intramolecular association between radical cations of the viologen dimer is very efficient, while that of the viologens of the trimer is not.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the electrochemical and spectroscopic studies of viologen radical ions, which are model compounds of the electron transfer reaction of the photosynthetic reaction center.
the electrochemical reduction of the viologen dimer radical cation and the trimer radical cation, which are prepared electrochemically.
the synthesis of viologen dimer radical cations and their electrochemical and spectroscopic studies.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the viologen dimer radical cation is a dimer in the ground state but a monomer in the excited state.

the intramolecular association is not so strong as to prevent reduction of the second viologen unit, but it is sufficiently strong to cause the second reduction to be irreversible and to shift it to more negative potentials.
the association constant of the dimer radical cation is larger than that of the trimer radical cation.

intramolecular association between the viologen radical ions occurs in a manner similar to that in the case of the viologen dimer radical ion, which is in good agreement with the results reported previously.

the association between viologen radical ions is not only important for the design of new electrochromic materials but also has implications on the understanding of the mechanism of electron transport in viologen-based molecular wires.
